steps.say: OS-PFX, rows QA-PAT-011..021 of docs/qa/catalogue/pattern.md (docs/specs/OS-PFX.md). 011..015 are the readout and the list (the simulator's pictures are the demo document's: the unit's shots are read by a person, the info line says CHORD 5A / ARP DOWN 4 STEPS / TUNE +7 ST / SLIDE UP 2.19 ST). 016..021 are the notes and the sound: the Chord / Arp notes are read on a MIDI monitor on the DIN or USB MIDI port (`amidi -d`, or any monitor; the scenario `pfx_midi` captures and compares them by itself) and the sample ones by ear or over USB AUDIO. The scenario writes to the loaded project in RAM only (nothing is saved) HOW THE VALUES ARE REACHED (OS-HILFIX): the FX picker (held Vol / Fx) changes only the TYPE of the cell and keeps its value, clamped to the new FX's range (our rule); it does not apply the FX's table default (Tune would start at 0 = -24 ST, not 24). So the steps below turn the encoder one detent at a time, from the value the FX before left. FX1 is edited with the held Vol key (+vol / -vol); FX2 with the held Fx key (+fx / -fx; `key fx down` / `key fx up` on the console), the same way.

steps.say: QA-PAT-016 (Chord on MIDI): give a track a MIDI instrument (Instrument kind MIDI, channel 1) and write on it a C note with FX1 = Chord 5 (`47`, Maj) at step 1, an OFF at step 5; connect a MIDI monitor to the DIN out (or the USB MIDI port); Play. Expect the monitor to show note-on C, E, G (+4, +7) with the same velocity at one instant, and the three note-offs together at step 5; Stop with the note sounding sends all three offs

QA-PAT-017 (Arp on MIDI): the same step with FX2 = Arp 6 (up, a note a step; FX2 is edited with the Fx key, not Vol: hold Fx (`key fx down` on the console), choose Arp in the list, release it (`key fx up`), then turn the encoder to 6 one detent at a time - Vol edits FX1 only). Expect C, then each step the note before ends and E, G, C ... start, ending at the OFF; Arp 17 goes down (G, E, C), Arp 28 draws at random from the three; Chord 0 with the Arp is chromatic (C, C#, D ... B, C); the automated check of the notes is the scenario `pfx_midi`

steps.say: CPU (docs/specs/OS-PFX.md, Real time): fill 12 tracks with a note on every step, `cpu reset`, Play four bars, `cpu` and `diag cpu`; then the same pattern with Chord + Arp on the MIDI tracks and Tune + Slide up on the sample tracks. The two `cpu` lines go in the report: no underrun in either, and the difference is the cost of the FX

CPU with the TB-303 module (the heaviest load the unit carries: the TB-303 song is about 70 %): load the built-in module and bind it to an instrument (`mod load tb303`, `mod bind 33 tb303`, as modules.json: a free slot, the console refuses a slot that holds a MIDI or sample instrument), give one track instrument 33 and a note on every step; `cpu reset`, Play four bars, `cpu` and `diag cpu`; then the same track with FX1 = Chord 5 (hold Vol) and FX2 = Arp 11 (hold Fx) (up, 8 module notes a step, the fastest rate is 6 microsteps: each a retrigger of the module). Read `underrun`, the worst block and any governor line (`mod`, `diag cpu`): none may rise, and the difference between the two readings is the cost of an Arp on a module. The Chord is there so that the Arp has notes: on a module the Chord alone plays its root only

MIDI traffic (docs/specs/OS-PFX.md, Real time): a Chord sends four times the notes of a plain step, and an Arp note is an off and an on of 3 bytes each; the DIN out carries about 3.1 kB/s (no running status, 960 us a message). Four MIDI tracks with Arp at rate 3 (value 11) are 3.07 kB/s at 120 BPM and more above 122 BPM: on a MIDI monitor the notes then arrive late and some are missing, the DIN being the limit and the sequencer not. Check once on the DIN out at 120 BPM (all arrive, in time) and at 160 BPM (late or lost on DIN, complete on USB MIDI)

steps.say: QA-PAT-102 (by ear, against a desktop player): import /MOD/kc_dancinonamiga.mod with the engine window OFF (the Modern engine: its 0xy arpeggio, Axy volume slides and E1x / E2x / EAx / EBx fine slides are the tracker FX) and /S3M/speed_chip.s3m (the S3M default: Jxy, Dxy, the fine slides) from the file browser; play them next to the same files in a desktop player (OpenMPT or any libopenmpt player). steps.say: QA-PAT-112 (by ear, against a desktop player): import /S3M/ompt_retrig_cut.s3m and /S3M/simpsons16.s3m (an S3M is the Modern engine by default: its Qxy retrigger is now the tracker FX 55 with the volume code, where it was a MED Roll approximation) and play them beside the same file in a desktop player: the restarts are on the same ticks, counted every y ticks across the rows, and the volume code changes the level at each restart as in the player. The Pxy pan slide, Ixy tremor, S1x glissando and the waveforms have no file in the test set: build one with tools/mod_build.py (the oracle's modules, tests/corefx_openmpt_oracle.py) and copy it to the card root as /S3M/cf2_test.s3m (never into the repository): P04 sweeps the pan from the S88 centre to the right over a row, I11 gates the note two ticks on two off, Q23 restarts it every three ticks.

QA-PAT-113 (parameter memory, host-verified): an S3M with D04 then D00, J37 then J00, EF4 then E00 keeps sliding / arpeggiating on the rows with 00: open the imported pattern and read the cells: the importer wrote the explicit value (D04 twice, 46 37 twice), not a 00. Against the desktop player the slides continue on the same rows.

QA-PAT-114 (pan, by ear with headphones): MOD 8xx E8x and S3M Xxx S8x import as Channel pan (FX 57, 0 left, 100 right, 50 centre; the Pan Slide Pxy goes on from it). A MOD with 8xx (any in /MOD/ with a pan command, or the module built for QA-PAT-112) moves a channel across the stereo field, and the pan stays on the notes after it, even for instruments with a pan of their own, until another 8xx or stop and play again (then every track is back on its instrument's pan at its next note). The OG export drops it (the report counts it with the other core FX).

QA-PAT-117 (the Panning FX, by ear with headphones): put Panning (FX 31) 100 on a note of a pattern, then a plain note after it with an instrument whose pan is at the centre: the first note plays hard right, the plain note plays at the instrument's pan (the FX ended with its step: our rule); a FX Off (01) step ends it too. Channel Pan 100 in the same place stays hard right on the plain note.

QA-PAT-115 (CPU): with pan slides, tremors and retriggers running on every track that has one, `cpu` and `voices`: the processor runs once a tick, from flash; the host bench puts 12 tracks with an effect each at about 0.2 % of the CPU at 50 ticks a second (an upper bound); the reading should stay within a few tenths of a percent of the same song without them.

QA-PAT-146 (volumes, by ear): put a held note on tracks 1 and 2 of a pattern and Channel Volume 20 (hex) on track 1's step, then play: track 1 sounds half as loud as track 2 and keeps it over its next notes until another Channel Volume or play. Global Volume 20 on any track's FX halves every track at once (the two multiply on a track that has both). A Channel Vol Slide 04 on a long row fades the track a step a tick from the second tick (a Global Vol Slide 04 fades the whole song); Fy / xF (3F, F2) move once. For an imported S3M with Mxx / Nxy / Vxx / Wxy (none in the card's test set: copy a module of tools/mod_build.py or any of your own to the card root) play beside a desktop player: the levels follow it (the oracle compares them per tick: corefx_openmpt_oracle.py chvol_*, gvol_*, 0 disagreements).

QA-PAT-147 (stop gives the volumes back): end a pattern with Global Volume 00 (or a Global Vol Slide that reaches 0) and a Channel Volume 00 on one track, play to the end, Stop, then play the pads of that track: they sound at full level (the volumes end with the stop as well as with the next play, so a fade-out song does not leave the instrument silent).

QA-PAT-289 (by ear): Play pattern 1, STEP (Rec), hold F1, pad 2, Copy, pad 1, Shift + Copy: the new pattern plays from the next row: at most one row is half old and half new, no sampler note hangs, the play line does not jump. A track's new length applies from its next row, but the pass in progress ends at the OLD pattern length (the pattern's length is read when a pattern starts): with a longer pattern 2 the pass is cut at the old end and the whole pattern plays from the next pass; with a shorter one the tracks wrap early and the pass keeps its length. F8: pattern 1 is back. Then the latent case (PAT-OPS spec section 8; not fixed): a MIDI track of pattern 1 with a long note, pattern 2 empty on that track, the same paste while the note sounds; watch `amidi -d` and write down whether the note stays on until Stop. The lane holds that controller's points at the ticks where the encoder or knob moved, the CC A row still names the same controller, and no CC lands in the step columns.
